To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ray aberrations of a phase plate illuminated by off-axis beams are strongly dependent on the defocus aberrations, which is not mentioned in previous literature.

the ray aberrations of phase plates illuminated by an off-axis collimated beam can be approximately described by the defocus aberrations of the collimated beam, and the ray aberration of a cubic phase plate illuminated by an off axis collimated beam is approximately equal to the defocus and the spherical aberrations of the incident beam.
the ray aberrations of the cubic phase plate illuminated by off-axis beams with a small derivative can be approximately described as a combination of spherical aberration and coma aberrations.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ray aberrations of a free form phase plate illuminated by an off-axis collimated beam can be approximately calculated by adding the defocus aberrations to the ray aberrations induced by the phase plate when illuminated by a collimated beam on axis.
the approximate aberrations can be applied to the design of phase plates illuminated by collimated beams with the field positions and defocus aberrations taken into account.
the defocus aberrations should be taken into account in the design of phase coded imaging systems, and the field dependent aberrations can be neglected for small derivative phase plates.
